```{r setup}
library(clintrace)
library(dplyr)
```

## Overview

This vignette shows patterns suitable for production clinical programming:
wrapping derivation functions, attaching lineage to datasets, validating
completeness, and exporting metadata for Define-XML.

## 1. Wrapping derivation functions

Use `wrap_derive()` around any function that creates analysis variables
(including admiral functions or company-specific helpers).

```{r}
dm <- load_example("dm")

# Example function (replace with admiral::derive_vars_... in real use)
derive_age_groups <- function(dataset) {
  dataset %>%
    mutate(
      AGEGR1 = case_when(
        AGE < 65 ~ "<65",
        AGE < 75 ~ "65-74",
        TRUE     ~ ">=75"
      ),
      AGEGR1N = case_when(
        AGE < 65 ~ 1L,
        AGE < 75 ~ 2L,
        TRUE     ~ 3L
      )
    )
}

res <- wrap_derive(
  data = dm,
  trace = new_trace(study_id = "ABC-123"),
  fun = derive_age_groups,
  target_vars = c("AGEGR1", "AGEGR1N"),
  source_dataset = "DM",
  source_vars = c(AGEGR1 = "AGE", AGEGR1N = "AGE"),
  algorithm = c(
    AGEGR1  = "Age grouped into <65 / 65-74 / >=75 per SAP",
    AGEGR1N = "Numeric version of AGEGR1"
  ),
  target_dataset = "ADSL"
)

adsl <- res$data
tr   <- res$trace

head(adsl[, c("USUBJID", "AGE", "AGEGR1", "AGEGR1N")])
```

## 2. Attach lineage to the dataset

```{r}
adsl <- attach_trace(adsl, tr)

# Later in QC or reporting
retrieved_trace <- get_trace(adsl)
trace_summary(retrieved_trace)
```

## 3. Validation

```{r}
val <- validate_trace(tr)
val$valid
if (!val$valid) print(val$issues)
```

## 4. Define-XML / ADRG metadata export

```{r}
meta <- export_define_metadata(tr)
meta[, c("Variable", "Origin", "Method")]
```

You can write this to CSV and feed it into your Define-XML generation process:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
write_define_metadata(tr, "adsl_define_methods.csv")
```

## 5. HTML report for QC package

```{r, eval = FALSE}
trace_report(
  tr,
  file = "adsl_lineage_report.html",
  title = "ADSL Lineage Report — ABC-123",
  study_info = list(
    Protocol = "ABC-123",
    Phase = "3",
    Population = "Safety"
  )
)
```

## Integration notes for admiral users

In a real admiral workflow you would typically:

1. Call admiral derivation functions as usual.
2. Immediately wrap the result (or the function itself) with `wrap_derive()`
   or call `add_lineage()` for the key variables created.
3. Attach the final trace object to the ADaM dataset with `attach_trace()`.
4. Run `validate_trace()` as part of your QC checklist.
5. Export `export_define_metadata()` output for the ADRG / Define-XML.

This keeps lineage capture incremental and does not require rewriting existing
derivation code.
